name: Amazon SimpleDB
tagline: AWS's original 2007 schemaless attribute store; still running but frozen in time.
description: Amazon SimpleDB is one of AWS's earliest data services. It is a schemaless store of items with multi-valued string attributes, grouped into domains, that indexes every attribute automatically and offers a SQL-like Select with eventual or consistent reads. Domains are capped at 10 GB, values are strings (so numbers need zero-padding to sort), and throughput per domain is modest, which is why AWS built DynamoDB as its successor in 2012. SimpleDB still works for existing users through the API, but it has seen no meaningful feature work in over a decade and is not in the AWS console.
statusNote: Still operating for existing users via the API, but frozen for over a decade with no console support; DynamoDB is AWS's NoSQL successor.

pricing.notes: Billed per machine-hour of request processing, storage and data transfer.

scale.notes: 10 GB and 1 billion attributes per domain; scale out by partitioning data across domains in the application.

strengths: No servers or capacity to manage
Conditional puts and consistent reads when needed
weaknesses: 10 GB per domain and low per-domain throughput
All values are strings; numeric sorting needs padding tricks
No feature development and no console support
useCases: Maintaining legacy AWS applications built on it
Tiny metadata stores in old systems
